title: codex-review.mjs builds its whole run state, parses argv and installs exit handlers the moment it loads, so the only way to run or test it is as a child process.
evidence: (a) Loading the file parses process.argv (tools/codex-review.mjs:251) and runs git rev-parse (:264). It can call process.exit at load. It declares about 25 module lets (:331-351: recordCopy, symlinks, keep, work, files, secretFiles, purge, valueChecked, secretValues and more) plus sets. It registers an exit cleanup and signal handlers (:355-364). (b) All of it is read and written by later top-level code in the same 1483-line file, and the exit hook at :355 reads work, keep, purge and valueChecked. Nothing imports the file. tools/codex-review.test.ts:65 and others spawn it with spawnSync('node', [WRAPPER, ...]), and the TEST_RUN env switch (:321-324) is a test seam read at load. (c) Owner: a main(argv) that builds one run object {work, files, secretValues, keep, purge...} and returns an exit code, called only under an is-entry check, with cleanup(run) called from one try/finally. The bare lets and the env-driven TEST_RUN branch could then go, and the logic could be tested in-process. (d) Risk: an accidental import from a test or tool would parse the test runner's argv, could exit the process and leaves exit handlers behind. Cleanup safety depends on lets that any line in 1483 can reassign.
